title: Show a timer when locked out for a period of time due to PAM policies
line: After too many failed attempts, the lock screen now keeps showing how many minutes are left before you can try again, counting down.
explanation: When pam_faillock locks the account, it sends the greeter two info messages at the start of each attempt: 'The account is locked due to 3 failed logins.' and '(10 minutes left to unlock)'. The lock screen showed them like any other message, so the time never changed and the whole note disappeared after 3 seconds, leaving no hint of how long to wait. The greeter now recognizes the 'minutes left' message (matched against Linux-PAM's own translations, so it works in every language), keeps the end time and exposes a live lockoutMinutesLeft that is cleared when it runs out or when PAM asks for the password again without a lockout message. The lock screen shows it as a persistent 'Try again in N minutes' line.

commits.message:
greeter: expose how long a PAM faillock lockout lasts

pam_faillock says only once how many minutes are left until the account
unlocks, so the lock screen showed a static note that soon disappeared.
The greeter now recognizes that message and exposes a live countdown.

BUG: 509286

lockscreen: show how long until unlocking is possible again

When PAM locked the account out after too many failed attempts, the lock
screen only flashed how many minutes were left and then forgot about it.
It now keeps showing "Try again in N minutes" and counts down over time.

BUG: 509286

media.caption: Before: right after the third failed attempt, PAM's note says 10 minutes
After: same moment, the minutes are shown as a 'Try again in 10 minutes' line
Before: 3 seconds later the note is gone and nothing says the account is still locked
After: the 'Try again in 10 minutes' line stays
After, with a 150 s lockout: 3, 2, 1 minute at 0, 70, 130 and 160 s, then the line goes away
